pull.title: GUARDED_BY annotations for nTx, m_chain_tx_count
pull.body: The cs_main requirement was never made explicit. The nTx field is modified when the block data is received and m_chain_tx_count is modified when all ancestors' block data has been received. Because of this, reading nTx from the getblockheader RPC may race as it does not acquire cs_main. Also, m_chain_tx_count may race in getchaintxstats if a pruned node redownloads a block via getblockfrompeer or if the node is running assumeutxo and tries to read m_chain_tx_count while it is being written to.

events.message:
GUARDED_BY annotations for CBlockIndex's nTx, m_chain_tx_count

The requirement was never made explicit. The nTx field is modified
when the block data is received and m_chain_tx_count is modified
when all ancestors' block data has been received. Because of this,
reading nTx from the getblockheader RPC may race as it does not
acquire cs_main. Also, m_chain_tx_count may race in getchaintxstats
if a pruned node redownloads a block via getblockfrompeer or if
the node is running assumeutxo and tries to read m_chain_tx_count
while it is being written to.

comments.body: micro nit: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36876/changes#diff-decae4be02fb8a47ab4557fe74a9cb853bdfa3ec0fa1b515c0a1e5de91f4ad0bR197 above says it's not held, but now it is. Seems to mostly impact REST, didn't checkmark it.
Yes, also the comment seems to imply that the function won't lock which is false. Should I remove the comment and the `AssertLockNotHeld`?
Done in ad6d75b196d301f1bfe430b8d05a23c70b5ea64a, which also removed the `LOCKS_EXCLUDED` macros

Hm, I'm a bit confused by this. `blockToJSON` already was grabbing `cs_main` inside of it, but still it had the annotation here. So was this a mistake? Otherwise it would seem fine to just leave them for both since just adding the lock grabbing to `blockheaderToJSON` doesn't seem like the right argument to remove it. We seem to have an example for this in the developer notes even for the `PreciousBlock()`: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/developer-notes.md?plain=1#L1056 And there are a couple of other functions that do this too. While this is not as critical here as elsewhere, the performance argument from the deleted comment probably still holds?

This was added in faea56400d5578023133cf4d1c761cdeb0c3e3da. The annotation just says that the *caller* must not hold the given capabilities. It doesn't say anything about the function itself.

Anything is fine here. It can be dropped, or it can be kept.
Thanks, this was poor justification, I was confused by the comment. I've reverted it in the latest push.
